cues.en: So let's go back to Spyder, and if you still have the contents of the Deep Learning folder opened up,
cues.zh: 回到 Spyder，如果仍開著 DeepLearning 資料夾內容，

cues.en: you should be able to select the auto wreck dot PY file. There it is. Like our RBM example, our implementation
cues.zh: 應該能選 AutoRec.py，就這裡。像 RBM 範例，我們的推薦自編碼器實作，

cues.en: of using an auto encoder for recommendations uses tensor flow and it's structured in much the same way.
cues.zh: 使用 TensorFlow，結構也非常類似。

cues.en: As a reminder, an auto encoder is just a three layer neural network with an input layer, a hidden layer and an output layer.
cues.zh: 提醒一下，自編碼器就是三層神經網路，輸入層、隱藏層、輸出層。

cues.en: Learning the weights between the input and hidden layer is called encoding, and reconstructing predictions with the weights between the hidden layer and the output layer is called decoding. But fundamentally,
cues.zh: 學習輸入與隱藏層間權重，叫編碼；用隱藏與輸出層間權重重建預測，叫解碼。但本質上，

cues.en: it's just a neural network with one hidden layer.
cues.zh: 就是只有一個隱藏層的神經網路。

cues.en: Let's skip to the neural net function here.
cues.zh: 跳到 neural_net。

cues.en: That's where things are fundamentally different from the RBM example.
cues.zh: 這裡與 RBM 範例，根本不同。

cues.en: It's not too complicated.
cues.zh: 不太複雜。

cues.en: You can see we're setting up the weights for the encoding and decoding here randomly initialized. These weights are learned and shared for every user we train the auto encoder with.
cues.zh: 可以看到，設定編碼與解碼權重，隨機初始化；所有訓練使用者，都學習、共用這些權重。

cues.en: We also set up a set of biases for both layers.
cues.zh: 兩層也各設定一組偏差。

cues.en: This is a little bit different from what the original auto wreck paper proposed.
cues.zh: 與原始 AutoRec 論文有點不同。

cues.en: They only had a single biased node shared across the entire layer, while we learned biases for each node which is more in line with modern practices.
cues.zh: 它們整層共用單一偏差節點，我們則每個節點各學偏差，更符合現代實務。

cues.en: Next we set up the layers themselves.
cues.zh: 接著設定層本身。

cues.en: Our input layer receives ratings for each item for a given user.
cues.zh: 輸入層，接受某位使用者對每個項目的評分。

cues.en: We construct the hidden layer by multiplying our input layer with the encoding weights and adding in the encoding biased terms, and then applying a sigmoid activation function to them.
cues.zh: 輸入層乘編碼權重，加編碼偏差，再套 Sigmoid，建立隱藏層。

cues.en: Our output layer applies the learned decoder weights and biases to what's in the hidden layer, and applies a sigmoid activation function to that final result as well.
cues.zh: 輸出層，對隱藏層套學到的解碼權重、偏差，最後也套 Sigmoid。

cues.en: This makes up our actual predicted ratings for every item for a given user the actual training happens within the run optimization function here.
cues.zh: 這就構成某位使用者對每個項目的實際預測評分。真正訓練，在 run_optimization。

cues.en: We use tensor flow to use gradient tape as we did in our low level example when we introduced tensor flow earlier in the course. It computes a set of predictions using the neural net we just defined and
cues.zh: 像前面低階 TensorFlow 範例，用 GradientTape，先用剛定義的 neural_net 計算預測，

cues.en: then computes a loss value by comparing the predictions to the known user ratings and computing MSE.
cues.zh: 再與已知使用者評分比較，計算 MSE 損失。

cues.en: Gradient tape defines actual gradients using a list of the weights and biased values we're trying to train, and then we call apply gradients using the RMS prop optimizer
cues.zh: GradientTape 針對要訓練的權重與偏差清單，定義實際梯度，再以 __init__ 定義的 RMSprop 最佳化器，呼叫 apply_gradients，

cues.en: we defined up in the init function to actually kick off the training for a given batch of user ratings.
cues.zh: 真正啟動某批使用者評分的訓練。

cues.en: You might try using more modern optimization functions such as Adam here if you want to tinker a bit.
cues.zh: 想調整的話，也許可用 Adam 等較現代最佳化函數。

cues.en: That's basically all there is to talk about here.
cues.zh: 這裡基本上就這樣。

cues.en: The train function kicks it all off in pretty much the same way as we did before with RBM iterating over multiple epochs and sampling batches at each step.
cues.zh: Train 與先前 RBM 類似，啟動一切，多個週期迭代，每步取樣批次。

cues.en: Let's shift our attention to the auto wreck algorithm file. There are a few things that have changed from the RBA example worth talking about.
cues.zh: 轉到 AutoRecAlgorithm，與 RBM 有幾個值得談的差異。

cues.en: First of all we're not modeling this as a classification problem where each individual rating value between zero and five stars are treated as a different input an output node. Instead, we just normalize
cues.zh: 首先，不把它建模為分類問題，不把零到五星的每個不同評分，當成獨立輸入、輸出節點，而是直接

cues.en: our input ratings into the range 0 to 1 here on line 31 and restore them to their original ranges on line 45.
cues.zh: 在第 31 行，把輸入評分正規化到零到一，第 45 行，再還原原始範圍。

cues.en: So we don't have to deal with soft Max and expectation values and all that in this example.
cues.zh: 因此，不用處理 softmax、期望值等等。

cues.en: As such, our input matrix that we pass into our train function on line 35 is just a 2D array of ratings between users and items. By the way, this is different from what was in the original auto wreck paper.
cues.zh: 傳給第 35 行 Train 的輸入矩陣，只是使用者與項目評分的二維陣列。順帶一提，與原始 AutoRec 論文不同。

cues.en: They flipped things so they train the network on items instead of users.
cues.zh: 它們反過來，以項目而不是使用者訓練網路。

cues.en: They would feed in all of the ratings by each user for a given item while we are feeding in the ratings for every item for each given user.
cues.zh: 它們輸入各使用者對某項目的所有評分，我們輸入每位使用者對所有項目的評分。

cues.en: Again if you want to tinker you might try doing it the other way to see if you get better results.
cues.zh: 同樣，如果想調整，可以反過來試，看看有沒有更好。

cues.en: Let's kick it off and see how it does. open up the autorec Bake Off file. There's not much to talk about and what it does.
cues.zh: 執行看看。開啟 AutoRecBakeOff，做的事沒太多說明。

cues.en: It just uses our framework to compare auto Rec to random recommendations as we've done before.
cues.zh: 像之前，用框架比較 AutoRec 與隨機推薦。

cues.en: Hit play, and it will take several minutes to do all of its work, as we've set this up to do all of the
cues.zh: 按播放，需要幾分鐘，因為設定成也做所有

cues.en: top end metrics as well as generate some sample top end recommendations, so we can get a more comprehensive picture of how it's doing.
cues.zh: Top-N 指標，以及產生一些 Top-N 範例，讓我們更完整了解表現。

cues.en: Now that it's done let's look at the results.
cues.zh: 完成了，看看結果。

cues.en: Let's scroll up to the table of metrics.
cues.zh: 往上捲到指標表。

cues.en: And the results are well, pretty disappointing.
cues.zh: 結果，嗯，相當令人失望。

cues.en: RMSE and m80 are both worse than random. although we've seen that systematically under or overestimating ratings can have this effect without impacting the quality of top nd recommendations.
cues.zh: RMSE、MAE 都比隨機差；但我們看過，系統性高估或低估評分，可能造成這種效果，卻不影響 Top-N 推薦品質。

cues.en: So we shouldn't panic just yet, but the hit rate is also worse.
cues.zh: 因此，還不用慌，但命中率也更差。

cues.en: Average reciprocal hit rate is a little bit higher, so the results probably aren't terrible, but certainly they don't seem to have been worth the effort.
cues.zh: 平均倒數命中率略高，所以結果可能沒那麼糟，但確實似乎不值得花這麼多工夫。

cues.en: Diversity and novelty are about the same as random, and our random recommendations are actually using a normal distribution to favorite popular items a little bit more. So at least we're not recommending
cues.zh: 多樣性、新穎性與隨機差不多，而隨機推薦實際用常態分布，稍微偏重熱門項目。因此，至少似乎沒有向使用者推薦

cues.en: super obscure or totally random things to users it seems.
cues.zh: 超冷門，或完全隨機的東西。

cues.en: Let's take a qualitative subjective look at the results as well, and scroll down to a sample top end recommendations for user 85.
cues.zh: 也主觀看看品質，向下查看使用者 85 的 Top-N 範例。

cues.en: These recommendations don't strike me as horrible, but they're certainly not inspiring given what we know about this user.
cues.zh: 推薦不至於很糟，但考慮到已知興趣，絕對不令人振奮。

cues.en: The only result that really seems relevant to this user's interests is Raiders Of The Lost Ark.
cues.zh: 唯一真的看來相關的，是《法櫃奇兵》。

cues.en: So what went wrong?
cues.zh: 哪裡錯了？

cues.en: I spent a lot of time digging into this myself.
cues.zh: 我自己花了很多時間研究。

cues.en: If you started investigating the actual rating predictions being made you'll find that most of them are very close to zero.
cues.zh: 如果查看實際預測評分，會發現大部分非常接近零。

cues.en: This tells me that all the zeros in our training matrix that represent and missing ratings are really messing things up.
cues.zh: 這告訴我，訓練矩陣中，代表缺失評分的那些零，真的把事情搞砸。

cues.en: We don't have enough actual ratings to prevent our neural network from learning that. For most items, the best prediction of a rating is zero, which means to us that the user never saw that movie to begin
cues.zh: 實際評分不足，無法阻止神經網路學到：大部分項目，最佳預測是零，而對我們來說，零只表示使用者一開始，

cues.en: with.
cues.zh: 就沒看過電影。

cues.en: Since our network can't distinguish between missing ratings and a zero rating, it just thinks that people hate pretty much everything.
cues.zh: 網路無法區分缺失與零分，所以以為大家幾乎什麼都討厭。

cues.en: If you were to throw enough training data at the network it might start to overcome that, but one hundred thousand ratings is nowhere near enough for that to happen.
cues.zh: 如果投入足夠訓練資料，也許能克服，但十萬筆，遠遠不夠。

cues.en: I've seen people get reasonable results from an approach like this with a million or more ratings, but it's still a fundamental problem that we're ignoring the requirement to only consider actual ratings
cues.zh: 我看過有人用一百萬筆以上，得到合理結果，但我們忽略訓練時，只考慮實際評分的要求，仍是根本

cues.en: while training the network. I spent a bunch of time tuning the hyper parameters such as the learning rate and the number of hidden nodes.
cues.zh: 問題。我花了很多時間調整學習率、隱藏節點數等超參數，

cues.en: And it didn't help much. Any improvements to RMSE were purely artificial, because our code discards rating predictions that are too close to zero, and those don't count toward RMSE. If you want some
cues.zh: 沒太大幫助。RMSE 改善都是人為的，因為程式會丟棄太接近零的預測，不算進 RMSE。如果想

cues.en: more hands on practice with tensor flow however, it would be a good exercise to try fiddling with those parameters yourself and also to try a deeper neural networks.
cues.zh: 多練 TensorFlow，自己調整參數，或試更深網路，是不錯練習。

cues.en: What happens if you have two hidden layers instead of one?
cues.zh: 如果隱藏層從一變兩層，會怎樣？

cues.en: It's not too hard to wire that extra layer in.
cues.zh: 加那一層不太難。

cues.en: So consider that a challenge.
cues.zh: 把它當挑戰。

cues.en: Don't expect the results to be much better though.
cues.zh: 但別預期結果會好太多。

cues.en: Our fundamental problems here are the sparsity of our training data, and not having enough of it to begin with. A more complex network won't help if you don't have enough data to train it with.
cues.zh: 根本問題是訓練資料稀疏，而且量不足。資料不夠訓練，更複雜網路也沒幫助。

cues.en: Remember though, all is not lost. Dealing with sparse training data and being able to train with massive amounts of training data are both solved problems.
cues.zh: 但記得，還有希望。稀疏訓練資料，以及大量資料訓練，都已有解法。

cues.en: We just need the tools we'll cover in our section on scaling things up before we can revisit deep learning and get results we can truly be excited about.
cues.zh: 只需要擴展規模那一節將介紹的工具，就能再回到深度學習，得到真正令人興奮的結果。

cues.en: We'll get there.
cues.zh: 之後會做到。
